title: Symmetry Breaking, Hysteresis, and Convergence to the Mean Voter in two-party Spatial Competition
reasoning: The paper develops a mathematical spatial model for two-party political competition. It analyzes concepts like Nash equilibrium, bifurcations, and voter tolerance from a game-theoretic and physics-inspired perspective. It does not contain any components related to evaluating or benchmarking religion, faith, morals, or ethics.
